meta.about: Inventory of every visible element of the RigCheck Android app today, for the redesign. Source of truth for the redesign map.
meta.generated_from: android/app/src/main/java/com/rigcheck/app/ui/** read by hand on 2026-10-25 (commit 68db012); `tests_referencing` was a grep of android/app/src/androidTest for the element's text; since #188 it counts the uses of the element's UiTags tag(s) per test file (uv run scripts/ui_inventory.py --refresh-tests). Brought up to date on 2026-10-27 (#188) for the elements #186, #182, #184 and #169 added since; the toast is not tagged (test_tag_new null) because it is system UI.
meta.size_basis: Sizes are what the Compose code asks for (fixed dp where written; a ~ value is an estimate from padding and text size; '(M3 default)' where Material 3 supplies it; 'wrap'/'fill' otherwise). They are NOT measured on a device. Region and order are reading order on a 412 dp wide phone.
meta.reference_frame: 412 x 892 dp, edge-to-edge, light theme only

region_vocabulary.header: fixed at the top, does not scroll
region_vocabulary.body: main area, scrolls if it overflows (except where noted)
region_vocabulary.footer: fixed at the bottom, does not scroll

status_values: merged (combined into another id; say which)
split (one became several; list the new ids in added_elements)
replaced (different control for the same function; say which)
meta.how_to_fill: For every element set redesign.status. For anything not 'removed' fill new_screen, new_region, new_order, new_width, new_height, new_style. Put brand-new elements in added_elements (id prefix = screen id). Never reuse an id for a different function. Leave new_text null unless the copy changes.
meta.test_tags: test_tag_new is the Modifier.testTag value of the element (UiTags in the app); null when the element is not tagged (system toasts). An element whose one slot holds several different controls (the Scan error dialog's next-step buttons) also lists test_tag_variants, one per control; test_tag_new then tags the area that holds them. Repeated items (rig card, breakdown row, history entry, offer card) share one tag and are found with onAllNodesWithTag.
meta.today_measured: Measured on the emulator by the layout capture (LayoutCaptureTest, #189; merged by `scripts/ui_inventory.py --merge-bounds`), per frame (412x892 is the reference frame, 360x640 the small phone, -font2.0 the same at font scale 2.0). x and y are the element's top-left corner on the display and width and height its size as laid out, all in dp, in the first captured state (in the capture's order) where it is on show; `visible` is whether any of it is on show there; `count` how many elements carry the tag there (a repeated item); `seen_in_states` in how many captured states it is present. null: never found in any state. These supersede the estimates in `today`, which stay for the designer's round.

elements.name: Title
elements.text:
Experimental Tool —
Not for Safety Decisions

elements.name: First paragraph
elements.text: RigCheck is an experimental project built to learn app development, not a certified or professional weight-safety tool. You type in numbers straight off your own tag and ticket photos, and the math that follows is simplified — any step of that chain can be wrong.

elements.name: Second paragraph
elements.function: Says do not use for safety decisions.
elements.text: Do not use this tool to decide whether your rig is safe to tow. Always verify actual weights and ratings using a certified scale and your vehicle's official documentation, and consult a qualified professional if you're unsure. You use this tool, and any decisions you make based on it, entirely at your own risk and responsibility.
